content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is high or trending up.
- Underestimate prices after sharp declines; adjust downward bias when sentiment is weak or negative.
- Lag in price correction: model often overreacts to recent spikes and undercorrects in the following days; apply a 1–2 day lagged smoothing to forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overshoot downward after strong upward moves; cap forecast declines below 5% of prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) and underestimate late (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric weighting or decay to recent data.
- Sentiment correlation: when sentiment > 0.6, reduce forecast volatility; when sentiment < 0.2, increase downward bias to reflect pessimism.
